 :JUDGMENT:
1.
This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for claiming compensation on account of death of Madhu Kumar T.V., S/o Venkatesh T.M., alias Venkateshappa.

2. It is the case of the petitioners that on 12.10.2024 at about 11.40 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Kolar Rural Police Station, the Accused was riding the offending Motor Cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-07-EH-5725 along with the deceased Madhu Kumar T.V., as pillion rider from 3 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 Kolar towards Thotli Village and near Hoovalli Gate and he drove the same in high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and the rider/accused has lost control over the offending vehicle and due to skid of the vehicle they have fall on the road along with the vehicle, as a result the rider of the offending vehicle has sustained injuries and the deceased/pillion rider has sustained grievous injuries on his head, forehead, left hand ankle and back and thereafter the deceased died on the way while shifting to the hospital.
Thereafter, the informant/Harish lodged complaint before the Kolar Rural police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.419/2024 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 281, 125(a), 106(1) of BNS and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
3.

It is contended that the Petitioner No.1 is the mother, Petitioner No.2 is the father and Petitioner No.3 is the grand mother of the deceased Sri.Madhu Kumar.T.V., and as on the date of the alleged accident the said deceased was aged about 26 years at the time of accident and he was working as Junior Officer, Production Departmental Hetero Labs Limited, Vemgal 4 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 Industrial Area, Kolar District and getting salary of Rs.25,000/- p.m. The petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- under different head of loss of dependency, funeral and obsequies expenses, loss of filial love, loss of consortium, loss of estate.

4 It is contended that the accident is solely due to the rash or negligent riding of the rider of the offending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-07-EH-5725 and the respondent No.1 is the RC owner Narayanamma vs Pranay Reddy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120542214/
2 and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
5. In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 is placed exparte and Respondent No.2 appeared through their counsel and filed their written statements.

6. In the written statement of Respondent No.2 Insurance Company, it has admitting that the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and the same is valid on the date of the accident and denying the petition averments in part and contended that the Petitioners have not furnished the particulars of the vehicle including the driving licence of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further it is denied having insured the vehicle involved in the accident.
The insurer liability is subjected to 5 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 validity of the DL and other documents as per the law.
Further it is alleged that there is no compliance of provision under Section 134(C), 158 of M.V. Act.
Further it is alleged that the alleged accident is occurred due to negligence and fault of the deceased and there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
The rider of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid driving licence, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident.
There is no liability to pay compensation to the pillion rider as per the terms of the policy.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioners have constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age,
income and occupation of the deceased and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and reserves the right u/s.170 of M.V.Act.
Hence sought for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal framed the following:-
:: I S S U E S ::
1. Whether the Petitioners prove that Madhu Kumar.T.V., sustained grievous injuries due to rash and negligent act of rider of Honda Hornet Motor Cycle 6 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 bearing registration No.KA-07-EH-5725 on dated 12.10.2024 at about 11-40 a.m., and he died on the way to the hospital?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Madhu Kumar.T.V.?
3. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
4.
What order or award?
8. In support of the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 is examined as PW-1 and got marked Ex.P1 to P18 and closed their side.
The respondent No.2 not adduced any evidence.
9. Heard the arguments of both side.

11. Issue No.1 : This petition is filed u/s.166 of M.V. Act  1989 for seeking compensation for the death of the  7 SCCH - 7  MVC.No.8197/2024 deceased Madhu Kumar T.V., S/o Venkatesh T.M., alias Venkateshappa.

12. The petitioners' in the petition have contended that on 12.10.2024 at about 11.40 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Kolar Rural Police Station, the Accused was riding the offending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-07-EH- 5725 along with the deceased Madhu Kumar T.V., as pillion rider from Kolar towards Thotli Village and near Hoovalli Gate and he drove the same in high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and the rider/accused has lost control over the offending vehicle and due to skid of the vehicle they have fall on the road along with the vehicle, as a result the rider of the offending vehicle has sustained injuries and the deceased/pillion rider has sustained grievous injuries on his head, forehead, left hand ankle and back and thereafter the deceased died on the way while shifting to the hospital.
It is contended that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

The Respondent No.2/ Insurance Company admitted the alleged accident and the offending vehicle was duly insured with it and its version is that, the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the deceased and not fault of the 8 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 driver of the offending vehicle and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
Further it is alleged that the driver of the offending vehicle is not possessing valid DL, FC and effective permit at the time of alleged accident.
There is no liability to pay compensation to the pillion rider as per the terms of the policy.
As such the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation and in order to obtained compensation the Petitioner has constrained to filed the present claim petition.

Further it is denied that the age,
income and occupation of the deceased and the petition is false and frivolous in the eye of law and the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant and sought for dismissal of the petition.
13.
The burden to prove the framed issues lies on the Petitioners.

Hence, in order to prove their case,
the Petitioner No.1 herself examined as P.W.1 and she has reiterated the entire petition averments and contentions taken in the course of claim petition in her evidence before this Court and also produced as many as Exs.P.1 to P.18 documents.
Therefore, there is no necessity to repeat those facts again.

In support of the Petitioners case and in order to substantiate their oral evidence, I have gone through the documents produced by the PW- Narayanamma vs Pranay Reddy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120542214/

Ex.P.10 is the II PUC marks card of deceased, Ex.P.11 is the B.Sc marks card of the deceased, Ex.P.12 is the Employee ID of the deceased, Ex.P.13 is the Salary Slips, Ex.P.14 is the Adhar Card of deceased, Ex.P.15 is her Adhar Card, Ex.P.16 is the Adhar Card of Petitioner No.2, Ex.P.17 is the Adhar Card of Petitioner No.3 and Ex.P.18 is the Bank Statement.
14. In the cross-examination of PW-1 by the Respondent No.1 she has deposed that she has not an eyewitness to the alleged incident and the public informed her regarding the same.

At the time of accident the Accused/ Pramod was riding the offending vehicle along with her deceased son Madhu Kumar T.V., as pillion rider from Kolar towards Thotli Village and near Hoovalli Gate the alleged accident occurred.
She has seen the dead body of the deceased in Kolar Government Hospital.
Further she has denied that she has not incurred Rs.50,000/- towards the funeral of the 10 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 deceased.
Further she has deposed that since from 5 - 6 months her deceased son was doing job in Hetro Company.

Further she has denied that her deceased son was not doing any job and not getting any income as alleged that and in the intention to get more compensation she has produced cococted and created Ex.P-12/ID Card and Ex.P-13/Salary Slip documents before the court.
Further she has deposed that her husband/ Petitioner No.2 was doing coolie work and she and Petitioner No.3 were home maker.
Further she has denied that she and other Petitioners are depend on the income of the deceased.
Further she has denied that in order to get the compensation they have filed the false case against the offending vehicle and filed false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely.
During the cross examination Pw.1 has consistently deposed on the lines of the petition/prosecution case and he has made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

15. The Respondent No.2 contended that the accused is innocent and falsely implicated by the police and in order to prove its version the Respondent No.2 has neither stepped into the witness box nor produced 11 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 documents and any how the Respondent No.2 cross- examined the PW-1.

16. On careful reading of Ex.P5/MVA report it specifies that the Motor Vehicle Inspector has been clearly opined that, the said incident did not occur because of the mechanical defects in respect of the said offending and unoffending vehicles.
Further the said Inspector noticed the damages to the offending vehicle and opined that, front left side indicator damaged.

17. On going through the Ex.P-7/Postmortem report it is seen that Doctor opined that cause of death of deceased is due to shock and hemorrhage as a result of head injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

18. On going through the Ex.P3/spot Mahazar it is seen that in pursuance of the alleged Ex.P2/complaint on 13.10.2024, the police have visited the spot and the eye witness has shown the Narayanamma vs Pranay Reddy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120542214/
5 spot and the police have conducted the detailed spot mahazar, in the presence of panch witnesses and during the mahazar the police have prepared Ex.P.4/Spot Sketch therein.
19.
On going through the Ex.P-2/ Complaint it is seen that on 12.10.2024 at about 11.40 p.m., the Accused was 12 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 riding the offending Motor Cycle bearing Reg.

No.KA-07- EH-5725 along with the deceased Madhu Kumar T.V., as pillion rider from Kolar towards Thotli Village and near Hoovalli Gate and he drove the same in high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and as a result the rider of the offending vehicle has sustained injuries and the deceased/pillion rider has sustained grievous injuries on his head,
forehead, left hand ankle and back and thereafter the deceased died on the way while shifting to the hospital.
The alleged accident occurred due to the negligence and fault of the rider of the offending vehicle.

20. The Respondent No.2 contended that the accused is innocent and falsely implicated by the police and counsel further contended that the alleged accident occurred due fault of the deceased and no fault of the accused and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.

21. Admittedly, the accused is the rider of the offending vehicle and further admitted that, deceased was dead due to grievous injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.

On going through the prosecution papers, FIR, Complaint, Spot Mahazar, Spot sketch, MVA Report, Inquest mahazar, Postmortem report and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 are specific to the effect that, the rider 13 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and she has supported the manner of occurrence in her evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.

It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions,
which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot lost control over the vehicle and due to skid the rider/Accused and pillion rider/ deceased have fall on the road along with the vehicle, as a result the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died due to alleged accident.
In view of the police records, it clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the deceased Madhu Kumar T.V., died due to 14 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 injuries sustained in the alleged accident.

Because, for the above reasons collectively, it is clear that,
the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries and cause of death of deceased Madhu Kumar T.V., noted in the Ex.P7/PM report would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

Matters being so,
the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 281, 125(a)
and 106(1) of BNS 2023.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the death of the innocent young man/Madhu Kumar T.V., aforesaid, as the Narayanamma vs Pranay Reddy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120542214/

Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/rider of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
22. Issue No.2 to 4:-

The Learned Counsel for the Petitioners contended that the deceased was aged about 26 years at the time of accident and he was working as Junior Officer, Production Department Hetero Labs 15 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 Limited, Vemgal Industrial Area, Kolar District and getting salary of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
The Petitioner No.1 is mother, Petitioner No.2 is the father and Petitioner No.3 is the grand mother of the deceased.

Further the Counsel contended that as per the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, the Petitioners being legal heirs and dependents of deceased,
each of the Petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of love and affection consortium and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition.

sentences.text: 23. On going through the Ex.P-14 to Ex.P.17/Aadhaar Cards of the Petitioners and deceased, it is seen that the Petitioner No.1 is the mother, Petitioner No.2 is the father and Petitioner No.3 is the grand mother of the deceased.
A grandmother can be considered a dependent in Motor Vehicle Accident (MVA) cases if she can establish financial dependency on the deceased, even if she is not a spouse or child.

While traditional dependents are spouses and children, courts have recognized broader definitions of dependency to include other close family members who relied on the deceased for financial support or essential services.

Therefore, if a grandmother can prove she suffered a financial loss due 16 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 to the death of her grandchild, she would be entitled to compensation for that loss of dependency, as such Petitioner No.3 being a grand mother of the deceased she also considered as dependent of deceased along with Petitioners No.1 and 2.
Hence on the strength of Ex.P-14 to Ex.P.17/Aadhaar Cards, it is crystal clear that the Petitioners are the legal representatives and dependents of the deceased.

24. The petitioners have contended that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 26 years at the time of accident and he was working as Junior Officer, Production Department at Hetero Labs Limited, Vemgal Industrial Area, Kolar District and getting salary of Rs.25,000/- p.m..

sentences.text: The petitioners relied on the Ex.P- 14/Aadhaar Card of the deceased, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is shown as 21.08.1998.
The accident was occurred on 12.10.2024.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 26 years one month.
Hence the age of the deceased is considered as 26 years.
25. It is not in dispute that the deceased died in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.

In the instance case the petitioners claimed that deceased was was working as Junior Officer, Production Department 17 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 at Hetero Labs Limited, Vemgal Industrial Area, Kolar District and getting salary of Rs.25,000/- p.m.

In this regard the Petitioners have produced Ex.P-12/Job ID Card,
Ex.P.13/Salary Slips and Ex.P.18/Bank Statement.

Perused the Ex.P-12, Ex.P-13/Salary slip and Ex.P-18 and on the strength of the Ex.P-13/Salary Slip the last drawn salary of the deceased for the month of September 2024 is Rs.18,300/- and accordingly the income of the deceased is taken at Rs.18,300/-.

The Petitioners No.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of the deceased, in view of the Narayanamma vs Pranay Reddy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120542214/
7 law laid down by the constitution bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157 in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethy and other.

Thus the 40% of the future prospects is to be added, hence the monthly income comes to Rs.25,620/- (Rs.18,300/- + 40% =
7,320).

Since the deceased is the bachelor, it is appropriate to deduct 50% towards personal and living expenses and remaining amount, i.e., Rs.12,810/- (Rs.25,620/- - Rs.12,810/-) has to be taken as his/deceased contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 26 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '17'.
Thus the claimants are entitled to compensation of 18 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 Rs.26,13,240/- (Rs.12,810/- x 12 x 17) on account of loss of dependency.
26. In addition, the Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Loss of estate and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of Funeral expenses.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2018 ACJ 2782 in the Case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram, Petitioner No.1 is the first mother, Petitioner No.2 is the father and Petitioner No.3 is the grand mother of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of loss of filial consortium and also entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- each under the head of love and affection.

In view of the Pranay Sethi's case the Hon'ble Apex court in the year 2016 has stated that it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards consortium for dependents and this sum was to be increased by 10% every three years and consequently as of 2024,
a sum of Rs.50,664/- is to be paid to each of the dependents towards head of loss of filial consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses caused by the loss of a deceased.

It cannot be in dispute that the loss of a deceased causes a devastating blow to the dependents and the degree of pain and agony would be at its speak and would linger forever it is for this 19 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 reason an adequate sum is required to be awarded.
This sum can also be increased every year by adducing the record date of the inflation henceforth.
Accordingly now coming to the matter on hand, the Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.19,000/- on account of Loss of estate and compensation of Rs.19,000/- on account of Funeral expenses.
The Petitioner No.1 is the first mother, Petitioner No.2 is the father and Petitioner No.3 is the grand mother of the deceased
are entitled for compensation of Rs.50,664/- each under the head of loss of consortium and also entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- each under the head of love and affection.

Thus the Petitioners are entitled to the following compensation:

Hence, I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative and Issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.

30. Issue No.4: for the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.29,53,232/-
(Rupees Twenty Nine Lakhs Fifty Three Thousand Two Hundred and Thirty Two only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
21 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 Further, Respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

 Petitioner No.1 - Mother - 50%

After deposit, entire share of  compensation amount with interest allotted to the Petitioners No.1 to 3
shall be released in their favour through E- payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and she has supported the manner of occurrence in her evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot lost control over the vehicle and due to skid the rider/Accused and pillion rider/ deceased have fall on the road along with the vehicle, as a result the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died due to alleged accident.
In view of the police records, it clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.
Because, for the above reasons collectively, it is clear that,
the accident happened due to rash or negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries and cause of death of deceased Madhu Kumar T.V., noted in the Ex.P7/PM report would be caused by a road accident.
A grandmother can be considered a dependent in Motor Vehicle Accident (MVA) cases if she can establish financial dependency on the deceased, even if she is not a spouse or child.
While traditional dependents are spouses and children, courts have recognized broader definitions of dependency to include other close family members who relied on the deceased for financial support or essential services.
Therefore, if a grandmother can prove she suffered a financial loss due 16 SCCH - 7 MVC.No.8197/2024 to the death of her grandchild, she would be entitled to compensation for that loss of dependency, as such Petitioner No.3 being a grand mother of the deceased she also considered as dependent of deceased along with Petitioners No.1 and 2.
The Petitioners No.1 to 3 are considered as dependents of the deceased, in view of the Narayanamma vs Pranay Reddy on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120542214/
7 law laid down by the constitution bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157 in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethy and other.
The deceased was aged about 26 years at the time of accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '17'.
In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in 2018 ACJ 2782 in the Case of Magma General Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram, Petitioner No.1 is the first mother, Petitioner No.2 is the father and Petitioner No.3 is the grand mother of the deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of loss of filial consortium and also entitled for compensation of Rs.50,000/- each under the head of love and affection.
